_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Taiwan (ROC) covering aboriginal Austronesian peoples, Dutch Formosa (1624-1662), Koxinga/Zheng regime, Qing Dynasty incorporation, Japanese colonial rule (1895-1945), Retrocession to ROC 1945, 228 Incident 1947, KMT martial law (White Terror 1949-1987), Chiang Kai-shek retreat 1949, Taiwan Miracle, democratization 1987+, Lee Teng-hui native presidency, DPP-KMT alternation, cross-strait tensions, and de facto independence amid PRC claims.

hdi.rank: N/A (not UN member, not officially ranked)

religion.note: Highly syncretic; Buddhism-Taoism-Confucianism blend; Mazu (sea goddess) worship; Longshan Temple; ancestral tablets; incense; folk religion dominant; indigenous animism; religious freedom

ethnic_groups.name: Han Chinese (Hoklo/Hokkien)
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; speak Taiwanese Hokkien (Min Nan); southern Fujian ancestry; migrations 17th-19th century; DPP support base; 'benshengren' (native Taiwanese) identity

ethnic_groups.name: Han Chinese (Hakka)
ethnic_groups.notes: Distinct dialect; Meizhou/Guangdong ancestry; settled hill areas; Hakka Affairs Council; Hakka TV; politically diverse

ethnic_groups.name: Mainlander Chinese (Waishengren)
ethnic_groups.notes: 1949 influx with KMT (~2M fled PRC); all provinces; Mandarin; historically KMT-blue; military/government elite; generational assimilation

ethnic_groups.name: Indigenous (Austronesian)
ethnic_groups.notes: 16 officially recognized tribes (Amis, Atayal, Paiwan, Bunun, Puyuma, Rukai, Tsou, Saisiyat, Yami/Tao, Thao, Kavalan, Truku, Sakizaya, Seediq, Hla'alua, Kanakanavu); mountain/eastern Taiwan; Austronesian languages (Taiwan origin of Austronesian expansion); marginalized; traditional names restoration

independence.date: De facto independent since 1949; officially claims to be continuation of ROC (1912)
independence.from: Status disputed: Taiwan maintains it is the Republic of China; PRC claims Taiwan as province; most countries recognize PRC under One-China Policy

country_profile.notes_unique: De facto independent but not widely recognized (15 UN members recognize ROC); PRC claims sovereignty, threatens invasion; US Taiwan Relations Act (1979, strategic ambiguity); semiconductor dominance (TSMC, 90% advanced chips); 'Silicon Shield'; Taiwan Strait crisis potential; 228 Incident (1947, ~20,000 killed); White Terror martial law (1949-87); Sunflower Movement (2014); only liberal democracy in Chinese-speaking world; National Palace Museum (brought treasures from mainland 1949)

natural_resources.notes: Negligible natural resources; economy built on human capital and technology; 97% energy import-dependent.

military.notes: Primary threat from PRC; US major arms supplier; conscription restored to 1 year in 2024; asymmetric warfare strategy.

infrastructure.notes: Taiwan High Speed Rail; excellent mass transit; 5G rollout advanced; world-class broadband.

climate_environment.paris_agreement_status: Non-signatory (not a UN member); follows targets domestically
climate_environment.notes: High typhoon and earthquake risk; rich biodiversity; many endemic species.

debt_aid.notes: Net aid donor; uses aid diplomacy to maintain diplomatic allies.

education.notes: World-class STEM education; PISA scores consistently in global top 10 for math.

diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Selective; work permits for skilled workers; SE Asian migrant worker programs
diaspora_migration.notes: ~700K Southeast Asian migrant workers; Taiwanese Silicon Valley diaspora significant; brain circulation key to semiconductor industry.

digital_economy.notes: TSMC, MediaTek, ASUS, Acer, Foxconn headquartered here; world leader in semiconductor manufacturing; Audrey Tang pioneered digital democracy.

country_profile.national_anthem: Zhonghua Minguo Guoge (National Anthem of the Republic of China)

geography.terrain: Mountain spine (Central Mountain Range) running north-south; western plains; eastern coast steep
geography.notes: Island nation in the western Pacific; Taiwan Strait separates from Chinese mainland (~130 km); over 200 peaks above 3,000 m.

economy_extended.notes: TSMC produces ~90% of world's most advanced semiconductors; 5th largest forex reserves globally.

health.notes: National Health Insurance (NHI) since 1995 covers 99.9%; one of world's best healthcare systems.

food_agriculture.notes: Food import-dependent; oolong tea globally renowned; aquaculture significant.

energy.notes: 97% energy import dependent; offshore wind targets 20 GW by 2035; LNG import expansion underway.

transport.notes: Kaohsiung is world's 15th largest container port; EVA Air among world's best airlines; scooter culture (14M+ motorcycles).

tourism.notes: Not a UNESCO member; night market culture globally famous; medical tourism growing.

human_rights_gender.lgbtq_legal_status: Legal; same-sex marriage legal (2019, first in Asia)
human_rights_gender.notes: Asia's most progressive on LGBTQ+ rights; first in Asia to legalize same-sex marriage.

security_stability.notes: PRC's stated goal of reunification is primary security concern; increased PLA air/naval incursions since 2020.

legal_system.notes: Constitutional Court active; indigenous peoples' rights recognized in 2005.

cultural_heritage.film_industry: Internationally acclaimed (Ang Lee, Hou Hsiao-hsien, Edward Yang)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Free and diverse media; vibrant internet culture; strong press freedom
cultural_heritage.notes: Bubble tea invented in Taichung 1980s; National Palace Museum houses world's largest collection of Chinese art.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Rankings within East Asia. Global semiconductor dominance; regional democracy and press freedom leader.

current_leader.name: Lai Ching-te (William Lai)
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: DPP; former VP under Tsai; former doctor; 'pragmatic Taiwan independence' advocate; Beijing views as separatist; continued Tsai's cross-strait policy

former_leaders.name: Tsai Ing-wen
former_leaders.notes: DPP; first female president; refused One-China Principle; cross-strait tensions; US support; same-sex marriage legalized 2019 (first in Asia); COVID-19 success; Hong Kong protests solidarity; two terms

former_leaders.name: Ma Ying-jeou
former_leaders.notes: KMT; rapprochement with PRC (ECFA 2010); first direct flights; Sunflower Movement 2014 (student occupation against trade pact); unpopular by end

former_leaders.name: Chen Shui-bian
former_leaders.notes: DPP; first non-KMT president; pro-independence; corruption scandals; imprisoned 2010-2015 (later pardoned); cross-strait tensions; bullet-riding incident 2004 (election eve assassination attempt, suspicious)

former_leaders.name: Lee Teng-hui
former_leaders.notes: First native Taiwanese president; democratization; 'Mr. Democracy'; 1996 first direct presidential election; Third Taiwan Strait Crisis (PRC missile tests); 'state-to-state' cross-strait relations (angered Beijing); KMT but later pro-independence

former_leaders.name: Chiang Ching-kuo
former_leaders.notes: Chiang Kai-shek's son; lifted martial law 1987; economic miracle; 'Taiwanization'; died in office; opened door to democracy

former_leaders.name: Chiang Kai-shek
former_leaders.notes: Generalissimo; fled mainland 1949 after losing civil war; authoritarian rule; 228 Incident/White Terror; claimed to represent all China; UN seat until 1971 (replaced by PRC); died in office; mausoleum; cult of personality; dictator

910.name: Austronesian Origins and Indigenous Cultures
910.description: Taiwan as the probable homeland of all Austronesian peoples, the diverse indigenous Formosan cultures, and the island before European contact — one of the most linguistically diverse places on Earth.

sub_clusters.name: Austronesian Homeland
sub_clusters.description: Taiwan as the origin point of the Austronesian expansion — the largest language family spread by area — from which seafarers colonized Southeast Asia, Oceania, and Madagascar over thousands of years.
key_events: Austronesian peoples begin their epic maritime expansion from Taiwan across the Pacific and Indian Oceans (c. 3000–1500 BC)

Spanish establish Fort San Domingo in northern Taiwan (1626, expelled by Dutch 1642)

920.name: Qing Dynasty Taiwan
920.description: Taiwan as a frontier prefecture of Fujian Province, waves of Hoklo and Hakka immigration, endemic ethnic violence, the camphor and tea trades, and the brief modernization under Liu Mingchuan.

sub_clusters.name: Frontier Settlement and Ethnic Conflict
